copy: Your child can use AI. Can they tell when it's wrong?
Most kids can use AI by nine. Almost none can tell when it's lying to them - and it does, confidently, in the same voice it uses when it's right. That second skill is the one that lasts.
No account. No email. Nothing about your child leaves the device.
Before you let your child try any AI tool, ask one question: where does what they type go? With most, it goes to a server. With this, it doesn't leave the browser - and one button erases it.
The first mission is free. There's nothing to sign up for.

No account. No card. No email address. Your child can start the first mission in about ten seconds - on a school laptop, on your phone, on a link someone sent you. If it isn't for them, you've lost ten seconds.
One payment. Nothing renews. Nothing to cancel.

Four courses, one payment, and then nothing happens again - no renewal, no reminder email, no subscription quietly running in the background. If it isn't right for your child, thirty days to ask for your money back, no form and no reason.
Fourteen missions, animated by hand. No filler lectures.
This isn't slides with a voice over them. It's fourteen animated missions with characters, a story, and a child working things out rather than being told them. Eight to nine hours of it.
